attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post. He states this himself and is not quoting anyone.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps all three elements: revolutionary framing with no explanation, repeating corporate narratives, and dismissing critics. It drops the rhetorical 'prove it for them' framing, which is not separately testable.

contract.note: Reading 'the media' as a broad tendency in mainstream coverage, not every article, is a fair ordinary reading. It is easier to support than a universal reading. Requiring a representative content analysis suits a claim about a pattern.

evidence.note: The headline sentiment study covers launch to March 2023 only. Positive sentiment and a focus on Big Tech do not show unexplained framing or dismissal of critics in article bodies.
One TIME article explains adoption drivers and quotes skeptical experts. It is a single counterexample and cannot reject or establish a broad pattern.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no representative analysis that measures the three alleged tendencies across 2022–2025 coverage. The headline study is early-period sentiment only, and the TIME article is one counterexample. Neither meets the support or the contradiction condition.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'multiple', 'exactly', the comparison with GPT-3, and 'months before' ChatGPT's launch.

contract.note: An informed reader takes 'exactly what GPT-3 did' as offering a general-purpose language-model API, not identical benchmark scores. That reading is ordinary and not stretched either way. The June 2020–September 2022 window fairly captures 'months before'.

evidence.note: AI21's dated August 2021 announcement. It offers Jurassic-1 (178B parameters) through an open-beta API for text generation, question answering and classification. This is a primary product record from the company.
A November 2021 Google Cloud/Cohere disclosure describing API access to Cohere models that generate, summarize and classify text. This makes a second company inside the window.
The GPT-3 paper sets the functional baseline for the comparison.
Establishes the November 30, 2022 launch date used for the timing comparison.

reviews.rationale: Dated primary product announcements show two companies other than OpenAI, AI21 (August 2021) and Cohere (by November 2021). Both offered general-purpose language-model APIs for text generation, more than a year before ChatGPT. That meets the support condition under the fair functional reading.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. The factual claim sits inside a 'should' recommendation, but he asserts it himself.

semantics.note: Splitting out the embedded factual assertion ('burns billions of dollars a year') from the normative 'should' is reasonable. The claims about use cases and a killer app are correctly left out.

contract.note: Requiring net cash burn allocated to the ChatGPT product alone stretches the reading against the speaker. An informed reader would take 'ChatGPT' as shorthand for OpenAI's ChatGPT-driven business losing billions. The contract's own ambiguity flags say as much. The product-level cash allocation it demands makes the claim close to unscoreable.

evidence.note: CNBC, September 2024: a projected OpenAI-wide 2024 loss of about $5B. It is a company-level forecast, not realized cash burn for ChatGPT, so it cannot meet this contract.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence is a mid-2024 projection of OpenAI-wide losses. It is neither a realized figure nor specific to ChatGPT. The contract demands ChatGPT-level net cash burn, which is unfair to the speaker's ordinary meaning. Even on a fairer company-wide reading, the packet has no realized 2024 result.

attribution.note: Zitron's own causal assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: 'It only caught fire because the media insisted' is rendered faithfully as a causal claim about why ChatGPT took off.

contract.note: Reading 'only because' as making media insistence a necessary cause is fair and somewhat charitable compared with an exclusive-cause reading. The causal-evidence requirements suit the claim.

evidence.note: The Tow Center/Media Cloud data show news coverage rising sharply about two months after launch, after 1M users in days. But it notes early coverage existed. Timing alone does not settle causation.
Documents heavy early user discussion on Twitter. It does not show how users found ChatGPT or whether that sharing was independent of media coverage.

reviews.rationale: The timing data cut against a simple media-first story: coverage surged after the early adoption spike. But the media covered ChatGPT early, and no item separates media influence from user sharing or product appeal. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.
